title: Marathon Ted Lewis session and the blues date with Spivak
summary: Long Lewis takes with Jimmy Dorsey and a later blues session with Spivak and others.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Since they made those things. You've made those down in Richmond, Indiana. Yeah. How long did you stay on that trip? Is that a day or two? Two or three days, I think. It took Ted Lewis with Jimmy Dorsi on the clarinet to make Ann Hague's children blues. We made it from 10 o'clock in the morning, 6 o'clock in the night, and we just finished it.

Really? Oh, yeah. Every time we'd get going good, something would happen. Yeah. Vandu would pop a string, or somebody would talk, or forget or say something, we'd have to keep making it over. Yeah. That was a fabulous guy, that Lewis. Yeah.

Yeah. Yeah. with Chauncey Morehouse, Charlie Spivak, Jimmy Lytell, Claude Thornhill, who made them on the Varsity record. That's when Spivak says, you know about the blues, teach me how to play a chord. He played a nice chorus of blues on there. I didn't show him nothing. I said, man, just play natural. Nobody can show you that stuff, it has to come to you. Played a nice chorus on it.
